title: Boss: Loop Master
summary: Four classic problems that need every tool in the module: decisions, loops, and input you cannot predict.

steps.title: Four trials
body: No new ideas here. Each trial combines things you already know: `if`, `switch`, `while`, `for`, `break`, `continue`.
They get harder as you go. Two habits will carry you through:
- **Work an example by hand first.** If you cannot say what the output should be, you cannot write the code.
- **Build in small pieces.** Get the loop running and printing *something*, then add the decisions inside it.
Trial 5 is a Sidekick piece: the planner behind `sk focus`.

steps.title: Trial 1: FizzBuzz
prompt: Read a number `n`. For every number from `1` to `n`, print one line:
- `FizzBuzz` if it divides by both 3 and 5
starter: // for every number from 1 to n, print the right line

tests.name: up to 15
tests.expect:
1
2
Fizz
4
Buzz
Fizz
7
8
Fizz
Buzz
11
Fizz
13
14
FizzBuzz

hints: The order of the tests matters. 15 divides by 3, so if you test for 3 first it prints `Fizz` and never reaches `FizzBuzz`.
Test for both first (`i % 3 == 0 && i % 5 == 0`), then 3, then 5, then `else` print `i`.

steps.title: Trial 2: The staircase
prompt: Read a number `n` and print a staircase of `*` that is `n` rows high and climbs to the **right**. Row 1 has one star, row `n` has `n` stars, and every row is padded on the left with spaces so the stars line up on the right.
starter: // one pass per row: write the spaces, write the stars, end the line
solution: for (int s = 0; s < n - row; s++)
hints: Count it out for `n = 4`: row 1 has 3 spaces and 1 star, row 2 has 2 spaces and 2 stars. What is the rule?
Row `row` has `n - row` spaces followed by `row` stars.
Inside the row loop put two loops one after the other: the first writes `n - row` spaces, the second writes `row` stars. Then `Console.WriteLine();`.

steps.title: Trial 3: Prime time
prompt: Read whole numbers, one per line, until you read `0`. For each number before the `0`, print whether it is prime:
A prime is a number **greater than 1** that divides only by 1 and itself. So `1` is not prime, and `2` is.
starter: // Loop: read a number, stop on 0, otherwise decide and print
// If any of them divides evenly, the number is not prime.
solution: Console.WriteLine(prime ? $"{n} is prime" : $"{n} is not prime");

tests.name: the edge cases 1 and 2
tests.expect:
1 is not prime
2 is prime
3 is prime
4 is not prime

tests.name: bigger numbers
tests.expect:
97 is prime
91 is not prime
25 is not prime
49 is not prime
101 is prime

hints: Two loops: an outer `while (true)` that reads numbers and breaks on 0, and an inner `for` that tries the divisors 2, 3, 4 ... up to `n - 1`.
Keep a `bool prime` for each number. Start it as `n > 1` (that deals with 1), and set it to `false` as soon as some `n % d == 0`.
The `break` inside the inner loop only leaves the inner loop. Print after the inner loop ends: `prime ? $"{n} is prime" : $"{n} is not prime"`.

steps.title: Trial 4: The guessing game referee
prompt: You are the referee of a number-guessing game. The **first line** of input is the secret number. Every line after that is a guess. Answer each guess with one line:
| The line is | Print | Counts as a guess? |
| a number below the secret | `Too low` | yes |
| a number above the secret | `Too high` | yes |
| the secret | `Correct in N guesses` and **stop** | yes |
| `quit` | `Gave up after N guesses` and **stop** | no |
`N` is how many guesses were counted. When `N` is 1, write `guess` instead of `guesses`.
starter: // Loop: read a line and work out which of the five kinds it is

tests.name: high, junk, low, correct
tests.expect:
Too high
Not a number
Too low
Correct in 3 guesses

tests.name: giving up after one guess
tests.expect:
Not a number
Too low
Gave up after 1 guess

tests.name: nothing is read after the correct guess

hints: Use `while (true)` and read one line per pass. Deal with the two lines that are not guesses first: `quit` (print and `break`) and not-a-number (print and `continue`).
`int.TryParse(line, out int guess)` returns `false` for junk. Only after it succeeds do you add 1 to `guesses`, then compare `guess` with `secret`.
For the wording, pick the word with a ternary: `string word = guesses == 1 ? "guess" : "guesses";` and print `$"Correct in {guesses} {word}"`.

steps.title: Trial 5: sk focus
prompt: **Sidekick piece: `sk focus 90m`** splits your time into focus blocks with breaks (the Pomodoro way). Your code
becomes the body of `static string FocusPlan(int totalMinutes, int focusMinutes, int breakMinutes)`; the three
are given. Put the plan in `result`, lines joined by `\n`:
- If `totalMinutes` or `focusMinutes` is 0 or less: `Nothing to plan.`
- Otherwise loop while minutes are left: block `N` focuses for `focusMinutes` (or what is left, if less):
`N. focus <m> min`. If time is still left, a break follows: `   break <m> min` (three spaces). After every
4th block the break is **three times** as long. A break never takes more than what is left.
- The last line is `<blocks> focus blocks in <total>`, the total formatted by **your own** `Sk.FormatMinutes`.
starter: // totalMinutes, focusMinutes and breakMinutes are given. Put the plan in result.
template: static string FocusPlan(int totalMinutes, int focusMinutes, int breakMinutes)

Dojo.Eq("70 minutes", "1. focus 25 min
   break 5 min
2. focus 25 min
   break 5 min
3. focus 10 min
3 focus blocks in 1h 10m", FocusPlan(70, 25, 5));

Dojo.Eq("the last block is shorter", "1. focus 25 min
   break 5 min
2. focus 20 min
2 focus blocks in 0h 50m", FocusPlan(50, 25, 5));
Dojo.Eq("exactly one block", "1. focus 25 min\n1 focus blocks in 0h 25m", FocusPlan(25, 25, 5));

Dojo.Eq("after the 4th block the break is long", "1. focus 25 min
   break 5 min
2. focus 25 min
   break 5 min
3. focus 25 min
   break 5 min
4. focus 25 min
   break 15 min
5. focus 10 min
5 focus blocks in 2h 20m", FocusPlan(140, 25, 5));

Dojo.Eq("other lengths", "1. focus 50 min
   break 10 min
2. focus 30 min
2 focus blocks in 1h 30m", FocusPlan(90, 50, 10));
Dojo.Eq("no focus length", "Nothing to plan.", FocusPlan(30, 0, 5));
// Given: your earlier Sidekick pieces (the reference versions).

require.message: Formats the total with your Sk.FormatMinutes

hints: Keep `left` (minutes not yet planned) and `block` (a counter). Loop `while (left > 0)`.
Each pass: `block++`, `int work = Math.Min(focusMinutes, left);`, add the line, `left -= work;`, and `break` if nothing is left.
The break: `int rest = block % 4 == 0 ? breakMinutes * 3 : breakMinutes;` then `rest = Math.Min(rest, left);`.

build.title: Focus planner
build.unlocks: `sk focus 90m` plans your focus blocks and breaks.
transform: // Focus planner: your own passing code from the code-dojo C# track (Control flow > Boss: Loop Master).
static string FocusPlan(int totalMinutes, int focusMinutes, int breakMinutes)
